verdict.rationale: Independent reviews credit the 285K with strong productivity performance and good power consumption and efficiency, including relaxed cooling needs and much better efficiency than the 14900K. AMD's 9950X still leads on perf-per-watt, and the evidence pack contains no Intel-documented power envelope (base or turbo power figures) and no sustained-load or throttling data. missing for 10: documented power envelopes (PBP/MTP), independent sustained long-render or export testing showing no throttling, a perf-per-watt lead over competitors.

support.subject: As a creator, long renders and exports don't throttle away — documented power envelopes and independent testing showing strong sustained performance per watt

citations.quote: Pros: Productivity performance, Power consumption and efficiency, Support for CUDIMM memory, Relaxed cooling requirements
Intel's Core Ultra 9 285K makes strong gains in productivity workloads
Compared to its predecessor, 14900K, it ends up both faster (barring some outliers) and significantly more power efficient.
